walkthroughs.body_html: Hajj is the fifth Pillar. Every Muslim who is physically and financially able must make this pilgrimage to Mecca at least once in their life. It takes place during the Islamic month of Dhul Hijjah. Millions of Muslims gather from across the world.

Pilgrims wear simple white clothes (ihram) to show equality. They walk seven times around the Kaaba (tawaf), walk between two hills (Safa and Marwah), stand in prayer on the plain of Arafat, and symbolically stone pillars representing the devil.
Many Hajj rituals remember the prophet Ibrahim (Abraham), his wife Hajar, and his son Ismail. Hajj is also a powerful reminder that all Muslims are equal before God — rich or poor, from any country.
